summary: Surface architecture for the selected work-order-rail chat Surface: focal outcome is the current assistant answer with its tool trace; T1/T2/T3 tiers, one-well-per-ticket disclosure with cite-back, four-breakpoint responsive model with keep-status/hide-duration and sticky composer, full keyboard/live-region/44px contracts, and an exhaustive state matrix covering conversation, trace, spine, composer, wings, drawers, reduced motion, and offline stub behavior.

claims.claim: Focal outcome is the current assistant answer with its attached tool trace, not the composer or the wings
Primary actions are send, follow-up pick, mode toggle, session switch; secondary actions are project switch, wing-view switch, tool expand, retry/dismiss
Information tiers are T1 conversation+composer, T2 session switcher+tool summaries, T3 tool detail+wing content
Hierarchy is spine -> ticket head -> prose -> tool rows -> well -> composer, with left resume wing and right evidence wing as session-scoped attachments
Disclosure rule: at most one well open per ticket, tool summary always visible, detail only on expansion, cite-back stamp in every well and wing header
Responsive behavior is 1440 docked workbench; <=1180 evidence drawer; <=820 left drawer plus sticky composer plus footnote translation; <=480 strip-spine plus stacked drawers
Keep-status/hide-duration rule applies at <=480px: status glyph plus word persist, durations hide first in ticket heads, tool rows, and spine labels
Spine compresses at 20+ turns (completed runs to counts, failures and current job stay addressable) with jump-to-failure; strip-spine carriage hidden at <=480px
Keyboard contract: landmarks for three panes, tab semantics for wing views, focus trap in drawers, Esc closes topmost sheet, 44px minimum targets, visible 3px focus ring
Live-region contract: polite region for streaming progress and session scope, assertive region for failures, no auto-scroll yank, no toasts or auto-dismiss
Every assistant turn claiming work carries ruled tool rows or an explicit empty-trace box; failures persist in place with attempt-keeping retry and dismiss-with-reason
No horizontal page scroll at any width 375-1440px; sidebars become drawers rather than squeezing the reading column; composer stays reachable at every breakpoint

decisions.choice: Exactly one spine per active session; exactly one node per assistant turn in chronological order; user turns render as slim ticks, never nodes; scrub cross-highlights ticket, node, and wing header together.
rationale: Resumption starts with where-was-I instead of scrolling (direction thesis).
Single index prevents competing navigators; ticks keep user turns visible without inflating the node count.
Cross-highlight keeps spine, ticket, and cited evidence synchronized.
alternatives: Two-level index with separate timeline plus session list
No spine; infinite scroll with jump-to-top only
risks: Spine scrollspy is the highest build complexity in the winning direction; must degrade to plain anchor jumps if intersection observation fails.
revisitWhen: If usability evidence shows users navigate by search rather than by turn order.

decisions.choice: At most one well open per work order; expansion is an inset well inside the same ticket; tool rows are hairline-ruled rows, never cards; every well and wing header carries a cite-back stamp Turn NN / Kind target.
rationale: Enforces CARD-SOUP GUARD: depth means job state, exactly one elevated ticket per viewport.
Cite-back keeps evidence attached to the turn that produced it (per-session scoping differentiator).
alternatives: Detail in a separate modal disconnected from the ticket
risks: Builders may be tempted to card tool rows for emphasis; audit must reject any second elevation.
revisitWhen: If a tool genuinely needs side-by-side comparison of two expansions (no evidence for this today).

decisions.choice: Keep-status/hide-duration: at <=480px every status persists as color plus glyph plus word; durations hide first in ticket heads, tool rows, and spine labels; ticket heads roll up to a status rollup line.
rationale: Repairs the known A-375px defect where tool-row status labels were hidden.
Status is product meaning (accountable delegation); duration is secondary metadata.
Preserves AA grayscale-safe signaling at every width.
alternatives: Hide status labels at narrow widths and keep durations
Truncate both status and duration to icons only
risks: Narrow ticket heads may wrap to two lines; rollup line must be concise (pill plus count).
revisitWhen: If strip-width testing proves the rollup line overflows at 375px with longest fixture strings.

decisions.choice: 1440 docked workbench; <=1180 evidence wing becomes tethered drawer sheet; <=820 left wing becomes drawer, composer sticky-bottom, wing meta translates to footnotes; <=480 spine becomes sticky top strip, drawers stack, prose stays at body size with 12px gutters.
rationale: Satisfies 375-1440px hard floor with no page h-scroll while keeping the composer persistently reachable.
Tethered drawers preserve cite-back context that a generic tab bar would lose.
Footnote translation keeps verification metadata reachable without a docked wing.
alternatives: Squeeze all three panes at every width
risks: Drawer stacking order and sticky offsets interact; z-order and sticky rules are specified to remove invention.
revisitWhen: If real-device testing shows sticky composer plus strip-spine consume too much vertical space at 375px.

decisions.choice: At 20+ turns compress completed runs to counted groups; failures and the current job always stay individually addressable; a jump-to-failure control appears whenever any failure exists; full expansion available via the collapse note.
rationale: Uneven agentic time needs spatial compression (burst-pause-verify rhythm).
Failures must persist in place and stay reachable; completed runs compress safely.
alternatives: Render all 30+ nodes at full size (long rail)
risks: Compression threshold interaction with strip-spine at <=480px needs explicit build coverage.
revisitWhen: If fixture sessions never reach 20 turns and the builder cannot prove the rule; then prove with a synthetic 30-turn fixture.

decisions.choice: Every drawer sheet carries a tether label naming its source (ATTACHMENT SHEET tethered to Turn NN; SESSIONS drawer; DISMISS WITH REASON for Turn NN) with the cite-back line Turn NN / Kind target; z-order is strip < drawers < composer; Esc closes the topmost sheet and returns focus.
rationale: Carry-in from D (cite-back stamping) plus B (tether/translation pattern).
Tether labels preserve session scope when the wing undocks.
alternatives: Drawers with generic titles such as Details
risks: Long cite lines may wrap in 375px sheets; mono cite line must wrap without h-scroll.
revisitWhen: If screen-reader testing shows the tether label plus cite line is redundantly announced; then merge into one labelledby chain.

risks: Spine scrollspy plus carriage sync is the highest build risk; degrade to anchor jumps with selection set on click if intersection observation is unavailable.
Drawer focus traps plus sticky composer offsets interact; trap must cover the composer while a sheet is open or keyboard users escape the trap.
Strip-spine at 375px plus sticky composer consume vertical space; prose must not shrink to compensate — gutters absorb it.
Staged determinate-feeling progress risks fake determinism; the honest stub label is load-bearing, not decorative.
Compression at 20+ turns is unproven in specimens; a synthetic 30-turn fixture with failures is required to prove it.
